title: Long-term and short-term memory in RL agents
abstract:
We discuss how an RL agent should manage its memory when operating in a continual RL setting. (By memory, we essentially mean the collection of various objects that an agent might maintain; see the thread for details.) For instance, one way of dealing with memory in continual RL is to maintain long-term and short-term memory components, e.g.

• Long-term memory: replay buffers, environment models, slowly changing network weights (e.g. permanent networks in some continual RL work)
• Short-term memory: an RNN's hidden state, recent history of the agent, fast changing network weights (e.g. transient networks in some continual RL work)
